A mountaintop hall of colossal pillars, each column a quarried mountain spine, the open roof framing thunderclouds, the floor worn smooth by centuries of titanic footfall.
A hill-giant rampart of piled boulders, each stone the size of a farmhouse, stacked without mortar into a lurching fortress that groans and settles in high wind.
A volcanic giant-forge of mammoth scale, its walls raw basalt slick with heat-sweat, furnace-mouths roaring in the dark, the mountain itself repurposed as a colossal smithing hall.
A great mead-hall with house-sized doors banded in black iron, its timber rafters the trunks of ancient firs, the hearthstone a flat boulder broader than a village square.
A thunder-peak fortress of raw granite, lightning-split and storm-blackened, its parapets broad enough for a giant to pace three abreast, the clouds breaking against its cyclopean walls.
A chasm-spanning stone causeway-hold, its bridge of mortarless megaliths bridging a gorge a thousand feet deep, towers of raw limestone anchoring each end like dropped mountains.
A ring of standing stones crowning a windswept summit, each monolith taller than a watchtower, the central hearthpit a crater of scorched earth, open to the howling sky.
A sea-cliff steading carved into coastal basalt, its titanic galleries open to crashing waves, salt-crusted stone columns framing a hall where the ocean itself thunders through the floor.
A subterranean giant-hold bored into the roots of a mountain, colossal vaulted chambers lit by glowing fungus, the entry passage tall enough to swallow a cathedral whole.
A tundra longhouse of stacked fieldstone stretching a quarter-mile, its sod roof thick as a hill, the interior a single titanic nave of raw stone and frozen breath.
A storm-giant eyrie perched on a sheer pinnacle, its walls the pinnacle itself shaped by brutal chisel-work, bridges of raw chain linking tower to tower above the cloudline.
A lava-tube steading deep in a volcanic flank, its cyclopean chambers natural and vast, rough stone benches cut from the tube wall, magma glow pulsing at the far end.
A forest-giant hall of colossal living oaks bound with stone, their trunks incorporated into titanic walls, the canopy overhead replacing any roof, the scale crushing and primordial.
A desert giant-hold of sandstone megaliths half-swallowed by dunes, its enormous arched gateway still standing, worn smooth by centuries of grit-laden wind, vast and desolate.
A riverstone giant-steading on a broad flood plain, its walls assembled from rounded boulders the size of granaries, the whole structure hunching over the river like a brooding colossus.
A sky-bridge hold suspended between two peaks by chains of wrought iron, platforms of raw stone hanging in open air, the wind screaming through its cyclopean grated floors.
A carved-crag citadel where a giant clan has shaped an entire cliff face into galleries and halls, windows like cave mouths, staircases cut into the living rock face.
A permafrost giant-hold of packed earth and embedded boulders, its walls as thick as a city block, the interior chambers low and crushing, smelling of cold stone and old bone.
A plateau-top enclosure of titanic dry-stone walls, open to the sky, each wall course a single row of enormous slabs, the whole forming a fortress visible from three valleys.
A cave-mouth steading where a mountainside cavern has been fronted with colossal ashlar blocks, the original cave extending impossibly far back, firelight catching the raw wet stone within.
A cloud-peak hall wreathed in permanent storm, its granite walls shedding waterfalls from every ledge, the great doors open and roaring, thunder rolling through its cyclopean nave.
